name: synfig
why: The command-line renderer turns vector animation files into frames, a niche but visually rich corner.

brief.what_it_is: The pages I read describe Synfig Studio, a free and open-source 2D animation application for Windows, Linux and macOS, built around vector and bitmap artwork with vector tweening, 50+ layers, a bone system for cutout animation, and linkable parameters. The brew entry calls it a command-line renderer that turns vector animation files into frames, but neither the homepage nor the GitHub README mentions a renderer, the synfig or synfig-config executables, or any command-line usage. Input is animation project artwork and keyframes; the output the pages describe is animation, not a specific file format or frame sequence.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it eliminates the need to create animation frame by frame, letting people make higher-quality 2D animation with fewer people and resources.
brief.how_it_works: The sources I read do not explain the mechanism in detail. The homepage says you set key positions and inbetween frames are calculated automatically, and that parameters of layers can be linked directly or through mathematical expressions.
brief.install_notes: The README points to installation instructions for Windows, Linux and macOS packages at https://synfig.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation.html and to building from source at https://synfig-docs-dev.readthedocs.io/en/latest/building/Building%20Synfig.html. The homepage offers a stable version for everyday use and a development version with experimental features. System requirements listed on the homepage: Windows 7 or later, OS X 10.8 or later, or a Linux distro released in 2012 or later; a dual-core CPU at 2 GHz or better; and 2 GB RAM or more. I did not read the installation docs, so I cannot confirm anything about the brew formula, first-run steps, or whether the CLI tools are installed by default.
brief.standout: It is a serious open-source alternative to frame-by-frame 2D animation, with bones and expression-linked parameters for building puppets from bitmap or vector art. Its homepage showcases work from the Morevna Project and other independent productions.
brief.status: Appears maintained. The homepage news list shows Synfig Studio 1.5.5 released on March 22, 2026, after 1.5.4 in January 2026, and the GitHub README carries a GitHub Actions CI badge. I did not see a last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The brew description ('Command-line renderer') does not match the homepage or README, which present a GUI animation editor; I found no documentation of the synfig or synfig-config commands, so the CLI claim is unverified from these sources. The README is thin and mostly links out to docs. Licensed under GNU GPL v3. Windows builds were noted as updated for 1.4.4 in 2023, so platform support details should be checked in the docs.

entry.title: Synfig
entry.tldr: A free, open-source 2D animation system where you set key poses and the software calculates the frames between, with a command-line renderer installed by brew.
entry.deeper_look:
Synfig Studio is a 2D animation application built around vector and bitmap artwork. It offers vector tweening, more than 50 layer types, a bone system for cutout animation, and parameters that can be linked directly or through mathematical expressions. The Homebrew formula describes itself as a command-line renderer and installs two executables, `synfig` and `synfig-config`. The pages read for this entry do not document those commands, so what follows about them is limited to the brew description.

The project's stated aim is to remove frame-by-frame drawing. In its own words, it "eliminates the need to create animation frame-by-frame, allowing you to produce 2D animation of a higher quality with fewer people and resources." You set key positions and the inbetween frames are computed.

The idea underneath is that an animation is a described scene rather than a stack of images. Layers, parameters and expressions describe the scene, and a renderer evaluates it at each moment in time. That is why a headless renderer makes sense: the project file is the source and the frames are build output. The homepage showcases independent productions such as the Morevna Project as examples of what the system can make.

The formula pulls in a large set of dependencies, including ffmpeg, ImageMagick, cairo, pango and mlt, which fits a tool that composes layers, text and video output.
entry.install:
brew install synfig
# The brew formula installs the synfig and synfig-config executables. The GUI app is documented separately at https://synfig.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation.html

entry.whats_unique: It is a serious open-source alternative for 2D animation that uses bones and expression-linked parameters to build puppets from bitmap or vector art, rather than redrawing every frame.
entry.caveats: The brew description says command-line renderer, but the homepage and README only describe a GUI editor and document no CLI usage, so expect to explore with --help.
